usage: I eat a lot of vegetables
examples: I eat vegetables together with rice.
nuance: 채소 is the general word for fresh vegetables and is a little more standard than 야채 in writing. Parents often tell children 채소를 많이 먹어요 to encourage healthy eating.
mistakes: Confusing 채소 vegetables with 과일 fruit
Spelling it 채속 instead of 채소

examples: I eat bread in the morning.
I spread jam on the bread.
nuance: 식빵 is plain square loaf bread that you slice for toast or sandwiches, not sweet bakery bread. Koreans usually toast 식빵 and spread 잼 or 버터 on it for breakfast.
mistakes: Using 식빵 for every kind of bread instead of just plain loaf bread
Confusing 식빵 with sweet 빵 like cream bread

examples: I buy rice at the mart.
I wash the rice before cooking.
The rice has all run out.
nuance: 쌀 is raw uncooked rice grains, while cooked rice on your plate is called 밥. You wash and cook 쌀 in a rice cooker, and then it becomes 밥.
mistakes: Using 쌀 for cooked rice instead of 밥
Confusing 쌀 raw rice with 쌀쌀하다 meaning chilly

examples: I eat rice cake on New Year.
This rice cake is very chewy.
nuance: 떡 is chewy rice cake made from pounded rice and comes in many shapes and colors. Koreans often share 떡 on holidays like 설날 and at celebrations such as housewarmings.
mistakes: Expecting 떡 to be soft like cake when it is chewy
Confusing 떡 with 빵 bread

examples: I boil the noodles in water.
nuance: 국수 means thin wheat noodles, often served warm in broth as a simple everyday meal. At Korean weddings people say 국수 먹는 날 to playfully ask when someone will marry.
mistakes: Confusing 국수 with 라면 instant ramyeon
Mixing up 국수 noodles with 국 soup

examples: I wrap rice in seaweed and eat it.
nuance: 김 is thin dried sheets of seaweed, lightly salted and toasted, eaten with rice as a side. Children love wrapping a spoon of 밥 in 김, and it is a very common everyday side dish.
mistakes: Confusing edible 김 seaweed with 김 meaning steam or fog
Thinking 김 is the same as the seaweed soup ingredient 미역

examples: I put cheese on the bread.
This cheese is a bit salty.
nuance: 치즈 is the loanword for cheese, usually sold as thin square slices in Korea. Koreans add 치즈 to ramyeon, toast, and rice dishes to make them richer and milder.
mistakes: Spelling it 치스 instead of 치즈
Counting sliced 치즈 with the wrong counter instead of 장

examples: I spread butter on the bread.
I melt butter in the pan.
This bread smells nicely of butter.
nuance: 버터 is the loanword for butter, used for toast and for cooking richer dishes. Koreans spread 버터 on warm 식빵 or melt it in a pan to fry food with a richer flavor.
mistakes: Spelling it 버타 instead of 버터
Confusing 버터 butter with 치즈 cheese

examples: I spread jam on the bread.
nuance: 잼 is the loanword for fruit jam that you spread on bread, and it is usually quite sweet. 딸기 잼, strawberry jam, is the most popular kind for breakfast toast in Korea.
mistakes: Spelling it 쨈 instead of 잼
Confusing sweet 잼 jam with savory 버터 butter

examples: I fry ham and eat it with rice.
I put ham in the gimbap.
This ham is a bit salty.
nuance: 햄 is the loanword for ham, usually sold in cans or blocks and pan-fried in slices. Fried 햄 is a popular side dish for rice and a common filling for 김밥 and lunchboxes.
mistakes: Confusing 햄 ham with 햄버거 which means hamburger
Confusing 햄 ham with 소시지 sausage

examples: I boil an egg in the morning.
I add an egg to the ramyeon.
nuance: 달걀 is the standard word for egg and means the same thing as 계란 in everyday talk. You can boil, fry, or steam 달걀, and it is one of the most common simple foods for breakfast.
mistakes: Spelling it 닭알 instead of 달걀
Counting eggs with 장 instead of 개

examples: I add beans to the rice.
The child picks out the beans.
nuance: 콩 is the general word for beans, including the soybeans used to make 두부 and 된장. Many children dislike 콩 and pick them out of their rice, which is a very common scene at meals.
mistakes: Confusing 콩 beans with 콩나물 bean sprouts
Confusing 콩 beans with 두부 tofu, which is made from beans

examples: I add honey to the tea.
I spread honey on the bread.
nuance: 꿀 is natural honey, used to sweeten tea, bread, and many drinks instead of sugar. Koreans also use 꿀 figuratively to mean something very good, as in 꿀맛 for a delicious taste.
mistakes: Confusing 꿀 honey with 설탕 sugar
Spelling it 꿀 as 굴 which means oyster

usage: I pour milk on the cereal
examples: I eat cereal in the morning.
I pour milk on the cereal.
nuance: 시리얼 is the loanword for breakfast cereal, usually eaten in a bowl with cold 우유. It is a fast and easy breakfast for busy mornings when you have no time to cook.
mistakes: Spelling it 씨리얼 instead of 시리얼
Counting 시리얼 with the wrong counter instead of 그릇 for a bowl
